title: Stress-test a source-backed summary
goal: Check whether a citation really supports the claim beside it.
explanation: A URL can exist and still fail to support a statement. For current/local news, use an actual web-search-capable tool and verify every link yourself. Publication time is not always event time. Without live sources, use the fictional fixture and clearly label it; do not pretend a model searched.
sampleInput: Fictional notice A, issued 20 October: “The community hall repair event is scheduled for 28 October, 10:00–13:00. Registration is required. Capacity is 40.” Notice B: “An earlier draft listed 27 October; that date is superseded.” These are fixtures, not real news.
prompt: Using only supplied sources, write three factual sentences with source labels and exact supporting quotations. Separate event date from publication date. State contradictions or corrections. If using live web sources instead, give a direct primary-source URL per claim and mark anything you could not open or verify.
workedExample: Supported: the fictional event is on 28 October, not 27 October. Capacity is 40. Registration is required. Unsupported: “40 people have already registered.” Capacity and actual attendance are different claims.

steps.title: Choose live or fixture mode
steps.text: Record which route you are using. Live mode needs current primary-source pages you can open.

steps.title: Extract atomic claims
steps.text: Split date, time, capacity and registration into separate claims.

steps.title: Request the summary
steps.text: Require source labels/links and short supporting quotes.

steps.title: Open and inspect
steps.text: For each live citation, check source ownership, publication/update date and the exact supporting passage.

steps.title: Record unresolved items
steps.text: Remove claims whose sources fail, or label them unverified; do not silently replace them with guesses.

checks: Every retained claim has directly supporting evidence, not merely a related link.
Publication date, event date, capacity and attendance are not conflated.
Fixture mode never claims to be live reporting or web verification.
commonMistakes: Treating a real-looking link as proof of the adjacent claim.
Inventing last-week news when the tool has no current search capability.
offline: Use the supplied labelled notices and build the same claim-evidence ledger; it is not a live-news exercise.
reflection: Which sentence looked cited but was not actually supported?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. Every retained claim has directly supporting evidence, not merely a related link.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Publication date, event date, capacity and attendance are not conflated.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Treating a real-looking link as proof of the adjacent claim.

editorialStatus: Original authored activity; independent subject-matter review and learner timing remain pending.
providerNote: Materials are free. External tools may require an adult account, credits, regional eligibility or a paid plan. Check current terms before using them. Do not paste passwords, API keys, private messages or other people’s personal data. No model runs locally or downloads automatically on this platform.
completionNote: Completion is a learner self-report based on saved evidence, not verified assessment or an accredited credential.
